title: Guardrail Runner — Ops Checklist and Incident Scenario Notes
content:
Overview:
- Quick notes for the ‘guardrail runner’ approach: a small ops-focused checklist + incident scenario catalogue to be used during multi-cohort LLM feature launches (canaries, phased exposes, A/B).
- This doc is intentionally lightweight — use when time is short. Pull from full playbooks (see linked_confluence).

Intended audience:
- PMs running the rollout
- On-call SRE and Release Engineer
- Product & Applied ML engineers owning model variants and fallback logic
- Solutions / Customer Success for customer-impacting issues

Quick glossary (short-hand used below):
- cohort: traffic slice (percent or user segment)
- variant: model or config being rolled out (e.g., gpt-lite-q4, gpt-3.2-32q)
- guardrail: an automated signal/threshold or manual checkpoint that triggers mitigation (reduce traffic, switch variants, stop rollout)
- fallthrough: user-visible degrade path (e.g., revert to baseline model)

Pre-launch (day -3 -> day 0) checklist — must green before any traffic
- Stakeholders: owner identified + backup (name + pager) — ACTION: confirm with Slack message and Jira RR-842.
- Experiment definition: hypothesis, primary metric, risk metric, rollback criteria — one-pager attached to the ticket.
- Signal contract doc: list of metrics (name, source, aggregation window, owner). Minimum set: p99 latency, p50 latency, errors (4xx/5xx), model-quality regression (eval set A/B), hallucination rate proxy (toxicity or assertion failure), tokens per response, downstream error rate.
- Dashboards ready: per-cohort, per-variant slices with time-shift compare. Perf and infra dashboards pointing to the cohort slice.
- Logging: must have correlation_id, variant_tag, cohort_tag on every request/response. Sampling: full logs for first 500 requests in cohort, 1% thereafter.
- Canary config: cohort sizes for waves (e.g., 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), spacing windows, and automatic gating rules.
- Automated test run: smoke (latency, correctness), regression eval (small prompt set), abuse-safety checks. Attach results to ticket.
- Fallback variant ready and smoke-validated (baseline model pinned).
- Comm plan: channel created (release-<name>-ops), notification list, and stakeholder cadence (15m standups for first 2 waves).
- Escalation matrix documented and contactable in Slack.

Signal contracts (practical thresholds — tune per product):
- Latency p99 > baseline_p99 + 150ms for 5m window => warn.
- Latency p99 > baseline_p99 + 400ms for 5m => gate and reduce to previous variant (automated).
- Error rate (inference 5xx) > 0.5% for 5m => warn; > 1.5% for 5m => gate.
- Model-quality regression: delta(primary_metric) worse by >= 3% absolute on eval set A => immediate manual pause and triage.
- Hallucination proxy: assertion-failure-rate increase > 0.2% absolute => investigate; > 0.6% => pause rollout.
- Customer-impacting errors (CS escalations) => immediate stop and stakeholder notification.

Note: thresholds above are starting points; must be adjusted per-product and historical variability. Document any changes to the ticket.

Runtime automation & enforcement patterns:
- A guardrail runner job (k8s cron or lambda) that evaluates signal contracts and emits actions: warn, reduce-cohort, revert, pause.
- Actions should be idempotent and always reference a reason code attached to change (RR:reason_code).
- All automated changes produce a Slack + PagerDuty event and write to rollout audit log.

Rollback matrix (quick decision table):
- Minor perf degradation (p99 +100–300ms): reduce cohort to previous stable wave and continue monitoring.
- Sustained perf regression (>300ms p99 over 15m) or rising error rate (>1% over 5m): immediate revert to baseline and create incident.
- Degradation in quality metrics on eval set: stop and run targeted failure analysis (sample logs + prompts), do not expand cohort.
- Safety-related alerts (toxicity, offensive content): immediate stop and notify Safety lead.

Incident scenarios (playbook sketches):
1) High p99 on variant after wave expand
- Triage owner: Release Eng + SRE
- Immediate steps: pin traffic back to previous variant (automated), collect 15 minutes of traces from GPU nodes, verify autoscaler activity, check queuing/backpressure indicators.
- Communicate: Slack channel, post status (impact: potential latency spike), update ticket with action taken.
- Postmortem: gather heap/traces, evaluate whether kernel selection or memory pressure caused stall.

2) Model-quality regression detected by eval set
- Triage owner: Applied ML + Product
- Immediate steps: pause rollout, tag sample IDs, snapshot model artifact versions, re-run eval with larger sample.
- If regression confirmed: revert to previous model; open RCA; test if tokenization/config shift caused issue.

3) Sudden increase in 5xx errors (inference infra)
- Triage owner: SRE + Release Eng
- Immediate steps: reduce concurrency (per-host), circuit-break traffic to baseline, rotate unhealthy nodes, check for kernel OOMs and driver errors.
- If infra issue: coordinate with Platform to apply hotfix or rollback runtime change.

4) Customer visible hallucination or safety incident
- Triage owner: Safety + CS + Product
- Steps: stop rollout, notify impacted customers (template below), toggle strict safety post-processing if available, schedule follow-up with Safety.

Communication templates (short):
- Channel post (first 10 minutes): "Rollout <name> — pause/reverted due to <reason>. Impact: <cohorts>. Action: reverting to variant X. Investigating. Owners: @leah @omar."
- Customer notification snippet: "We detected anomalous responses for feature <X> and have reverted to the previous model. We are investigating and will follow up within 4 hours."

Data collection & forensics checklist (what to grab immediately):
- Correlated traces (request id -> node -> kernel) for 15m before/after event
- Sampled inputs+outputs for failed requests (obfuscate PII)
- Model config + quantization flags that were active at the time
- Autoscaler and queue depth metrics
- Rolling logs from 3 most active hosts

Post-launch cadence (first 48 hours):
- Wave 1: 0.5% — 1:1 warroom check at 5m, 15m, 1h.
- Wave 2: 2% — 15m, 1h, 4h.
- Wave 3: 10% — 1h, 4h, 12h.
- After 24–48h stable: handoff from release to steady-state on-call.

Open questions / reminders (notes-to-self style):
- Do we have a standard way to derive baseline_p99 per-customer segment? (ask metrics infra)
- Need a short script to snapshot model config and push to audit-bucket on each wave (avoid manual mistakes).
- Can we add a small synthetic workload that runs against new variant to detect throughput regressions before user traffic expands? (runbook experiment idea)

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Rollout control UI: console.redwood.internal/rollouts/<name>
- Manual rollback (CLI): rrctl rollback --rollout <id> --to-variant <baseline>
- Snapshot models: scripts/snapshot_model.sh <variant> && gsutil cp snapshot gs://release-audit/<id>/
- Pager rotation: see Confluence on-call calendar (linked above)

Versioning & change log:
- 2025-11-04 — initial sketch (Leah)
- 2025-11-10 — added signal thresholds and incident sketches (Omar)
- 2025-11-18 — refined communication templates and forensic checklist (Priya)

End notes:
- This is intentionally pragmatic; codify parts that prove useful into the guardrail-runner code repo and canonical playbook.
- If you copy/paste thresholds into ticket, annotate reason and baseline used.
